I will keep the farm diversified, but I will not spread myself too thin. At my age, with 40 years of experience, I want steady grain for the household and a cash crop that I already know how to manage. I will keep stevia as my main cash crop because that matches my cropping system, and I have well irrigation, so I can support it properly. I will keep wheat and maize on a shared part of the land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize cycle, because that gives me dependable food and income from the same mu across the year. I will keep only a small area of cotton, because cotton takes more hand labor and pest control, and I do not want too much of it. I will also keep a small millet area because it is hardy and spreads risk if weather or prices go against me. I will use mostly improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stability, plough or rotary till depending on the crop, apply moderate fertilizer because I have irrigation and want a reliable stand, and I will not push inputs too aggressively. My goal is to protect labor, secure grain, and keep cash income from stevia without overloading the household.
